ruling: Herb jones DEF way too low all seasons
title: A WING IS SCORED AS A WING WHATEVER HIS SHOT DIET — the position rule yields to the card's own defensive shape, and the third and last place a listing decided a formula is closed

cost: THE SCOUT'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND THE ROUND SAYS SO. The shortlist put all four Jones cards on is_big's FIRST shape clause and proposed adding `rimprot >= perdef` to it. That clause ALREADY carries that test, it already fails for him (rimprot 65 against perdef 96), and it is never evaluated: `pos` is ['SF', 'PF'], so the POSITION branch returns 1.0 on the line above and no shape test runs. The proposed fix would have been a no-op. The defect is one layer up, in the position rule itself, and that is what this round changes.

NO NUMBER WAS GIVEN. "Herb jones DEF way too low all seasons" is directional; the orchestrator assumed 88 +-4 for '23. He lands on 91, inside that band, and the anchor is written at the landed value +-4. '22 and '24 land at 90 and 91, '26 at 81 on its weaker sheet.

WHY THE OBVIOUS QUANTITY WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED, and this is the round's real finding. The natural test is rim protection against perimeter defence - it is what clause 1 and recal_99's deterrence guard both use. It CANNOT separate Herbert Jones from two anchored genuine bigs: Dennis Rodman '90 (perdef 97 over rimprot 76, a difference of -21) and Draymond Green '16 (98 over 84, -14) sit on the same side of it as Jones '22 (-21) and Jones '26 (-15). Defensive rebounding is what separates them, and it separates them with a wide margin: Jones reads +79 / +71 / +69 / +54 on perimdisrupt - drb while every genuine big is negative - Duncan '03 -92, Rodman -74, Gobert -73, Sabonis -53, Garnett -40, Ben Wallace -18, Draymond -8. The gap between the highest big (-8) and the lowest Jones (+54) is sixty-two points, which is why a 30-to-60 ramp holds every anchor with room on both sides.

recal_72's WARNING IS NOT REOPENED. It hardened this rule and said 'Strict on both sides or the rule leaks', naming DeRozan, Korver, Maggette and Dunleavy as the cards that become bigs if the 'never PG/SG' half is dropped, and Paul George '19 as the card whose defence gets routed to rim protection he has not got. This round touches NEITHER half of the position test - it leaves the branch's condition exactly as it was and only changes what the branch RETURNS. All five named cards are unmoved, Paul George '19 included at 96 before and after, and none of them is a position big in the first place.

THE THIRD AND LAST OF THE SHOT-DIET DEFECTS. recal_93 fixed the middle shape clause (rim and 3pt deciding the branch), recal_99 fixed the deterrence clause (which still cliffed for shooters), and this round fixes the position branch. All three are the same complaint - a man's OFFENSIVE profile, or a listing derived from it, deciding which defensive formula grades him - and all three are now ramps keyed on defensive evidence. What remains a hard switch is the LIFETIME-GUARD branch (a PG/SG who is never listed at PF or C returns 0.0 with no shape test), and it is the next place to look if he complains about a guard-listed big.

THE TACTICS BANDS THIS ROUND BROKE. Both glass taxes went shallow on their BLIND edges again - crash off -0.22 and crash def -0.27 against a -0.30 ceiling - and were re-ratified through the harness: crashOff .10 -> .40, crashDef .48 -> .60. Chosen at the point of greatest margin (off: blind -0.41 / oracle +0.64, feasible .30 to ~.75; def: blind -0.36 / oracle +0.57, feasible .55 to ~.85). That is the third round running in which this pair has moved together, and the second in which they moved in the same direction as each other but the OPPOSITE direction to the round before. A round that moves any DEF at all should budget for re-ratifying them.
THE ROUND IS 103 AND THE PIPELINE IS 105. recal_99 and recal_102 took 103 and 104 immediately below this commit.
notes: WHAT THE RULING IS ABOUT, in one line. Herbert Jones has the best perimeter defensive sheet in the pool - perdef 96, perimdisrupt 87 - and was graded by the BIG mix, where rim protection 65 and defensive rebounding 16 carry 0.57 of the weight and perimeter disruption carries 0.00. His perimeter vector reads 80.2 against a big vector of 67.4. He printed DEF 76.

WHY A LISTING SHOULD YIELD TO A SHEET. The position rule is a good prior and stays one: _POS is the union of every position Basketball-Reference ever recorded, so it is stable, cheap and usually right. But it is a PRIOR, and one season logged at power forward is thin evidence against four seasons of a man's own defensive numbers. The override does not overrule the listing on a whim - it requires the card to disagree with it by a wide margin on the single act that is least ambiguous about which job a defender is doing.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool: 26 of 10,000 cards move on DEF, mean +4.00, max +15; OVR follows on 24; OFF moves on ZERO and no attribute moves. The top 12 by DEF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant, no leaver, no rank flip and not one member whose OVR changed. All 113 anchors pass.

THE OTHER MOVERS ARE THE SAME ARCHETYPE, found by the same test and not by a name: Luc Mbah a Moute '17 (64 -> 70), Thaddeus Young '14 and '18, OG Anunoby '25, Gerald Wallace - wings a box score once listed at power forward, every one of them lifted by being graded on the job he actually did.

NOTHING IS HALF-APPLIED. is_big is untouched, so Herbert Jones is still LABELLED a big on his card, still takes the big's o_ovr+40 cap branch and still sits in the bigs' marginal percentile class. That is the same seam recal_93 opened and named, and it is the price of keeping this round to the defect the ruling is about.
